Subject: Quick follow-up from today's trial demo (latency notes)

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo today. Our engineering lead ran the basic multi-region trials you suggested and attached a quick CSV with p50/p95 numbers from our side (region probes from us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). High level takeaways: p95 from APAC to your hosted endpoint spikes ~1200ms (we ran during business hours), US/EU looks reasonable. We also captured headers showing which backend was used (your header shows "backend: rwd-v2a" for some requests and a fallback to "rwd-small-compat" for others).

Before we escalate to procurement, our platform team wants a short validation plan: specific tests we should run to compare Redwood vs our current hyperscaler-managed endpoints (latency, cold-start variance, retry behavior under packet loss). Can you outline the exact test vectors and any configuration flags we should set on the Redwood side? Also — can you confirm data residency for request logs when using dedicated vs hosted?

Regards,

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -0800

To: Sam Harris <sam.harris@greenline-thera.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's trial demo (latency notes)

Sam —

Really appreciate the data and the quick run. High-level answers up front, then a short validation plan below.

Short answers:
- Test vectors: we'll provide a lightweight test harness (script + curl examples) that reproduces the probes you ran and records full timing breakdowns (DNS, connect, TLS, first-byte, tokenization time reported by our runtime).
- Backend headers: the two backends you saw are expected during trials — rwd-v2a is our standard low-latency variant; rwd-small-compat is a smaller compatible fallback we route to under capacity pressure. We'll include a routing pin in the test harness to force rwd-v2a for a subset of runs.
- Data residency: hosted API request logs are retained in our US region by default; Dedicated can be configured so logs and traces are kept in your VPC/region and integrated with your KMS for encryption-at-rest. I'll include a short matrix below.

Proposed 3-step validation plan (we recommend ~48–72 hours of runs per vector):
1) Baseline run (no pinning): replicate your current probes to capture real-world routing and fallbacks.
2) Pinned run (rwd-v2a): run with header pinning to the low-latency variant to isolate runtime behavior.
3) Degraded-network run: simulate 2% packet loss + 100ms added latency to study retry/backoff and cold-start frequency.

For each run we'll gather: p10/p50/p95/p99, cold-start count, token-level timing, and backend header. We'll also compute per-region tail variance.

I've attached a short validation-test-plan.md and a comparison matrix. Marcus will help coordinate a pinned-capacity window if you want dedicated GPUs briefly to remove noisy neighbors from the signal.

Proposed next steps:
- If this plan sounds good, can you confirm test window (UTC range) for next week?
- Marcus: can you outline how we can provision a 4–8 hour pinned pool for Greenline to run the pinned-v2a tests?

Thanks,
Tessa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
